# Experiments

Requirements extracted from [`SPEC.md`](../SPEC.md). This view is for focused reading and review; the spec text is normative.

## ER

- **ER-1** — **Core comparison.** Learned, classical and ER-9 control systems, full test split, every SNR in `params.channel.test_snr_grid_db`, at `params.bandwidth.headline_ratio` — which resolves to `params.bandwidth.crossover_ratio`, because a crossover claimed from a one-seed sweep figure while the full-strength intervals sit at a different budget would rest the project's most contested result on its weakest evidence (AM-20) — repeated over the seed cells defined by `params.evaluation.seed_pairing` — `params.evaluation.train_seeds` **zipped with** `params.evaluation.channel_seeds`, giving three cells, not their nine-cell cross product — reported with `params.evaluation.ci` intervals, measuring `params.project.primary_metric`. Rationale: the conjunction was ambiguous and the two readings differ threefold in evaluation cost; §16's decode-throughput estimate was written against three cells, and a third channel realisation of an already-frozen model buys far less than a third training run does (AM-17). Models are trained per DEC-11. Hypotheses are decided by §2 via ER-10. *(verify: results CSV + accuracy-vs-SNR figure, with exactly one row group per seed cell)*
- **ER-2** — **SNR mismatch.** Train once at `params.channel.train_snr_db_fixed`, evaluate across the whole test grid, and report the degradation profile of both systems to evidence the cliff-versus-graceful contrast (H2). *(verify: results CSV + figure)*
- **ER-3** — **Operating-point selection and bandwidth sweep.** Before the headline run, sweep every entry in `params.bandwidth.ratios` **with the classical system only**, on the **full validation split** at one seed, and select **two** operating points at G-8 by this preregistered, **learned-blind** rule applied at two thresholds: *the smallest ratio at which the classical system's high-SNR ceiling comes within `t` percentage points of its clean-image accuracy*, evaluated at `t` = `params.bandwidth.efficiency_ratio_threshold_pp` to give `params.bandwidth.efficiency_ratio`, and at `t` = `params.bandwidth.crossover_ratio_threshold_pp` to give `params.bandwidth.crossover_ratio`. Both are lookups against the same classical sweep table, so the second threshold costs nothing to evaluate, and the two MAY select the same ratio — in which case there is one operating point and `params.bandwidth.headline_ratio` resolves to it unchanged. Rationale for two: the looser threshold locates the **efficiency point**, the tightest budget at which the baseline is still healthy, which is where the bandwidth claim lives; but "within 5 points of clean" admits a classical ceiling around 0.83 while the learned ceiling is estimated at 0.85–0.87, so that threshold can select a ratio at which no crossover exists at all. The tighter threshold locates the **crossover point**, the smallest budget at which the classical ceiling can actually overtake the learned one. Reporting both shows the trade-off as a function of budget rather than asserting it at a point (AM-20). The rule inspects only the classical system at either threshold, so it cannot be accused of selecting for the hypothesis; it places the comparison where the baseline is healthy rather than where it is starved, and tightening a threshold hands the baseline *more* budget, which DEC-16's governing rule expressly permits. Because BR-4 now adapts modulation as well (DEC-16), the classical ceiling rises faster with SNR than it would under a fixed modulation, so the rule is expected to select a *smaller* ratio than it otherwise would — the crossover is bought with better use of the budget rather than with more budget. The sweep also reports `params.bandwidth.low_ratio_operating_point` as the bandwidth-starved regime where dominance rather than crossover is expected. Because the rule is learned-blind, learned systems MUST be trained at `params.bandwidth.crossover_ratio`, `params.bandwidth.efficiency_ratio` and `params.bandwidth.low_ratio_operating_point` **only** — at most three ratios, and two if the thresholds coincide — nothing in §2 needs a learned model at every ratio, and training five would spend roughly nine runs to inform a decision that cannot see them (AM-12). The sweep uses the full validation split rather than `params.evaluation.test_subset_size`: that parameter sizes a subset of the *test* split under ER-6, and at 2000 it exceeds the `val_images` count of every dataset in `params.datasets`, so the requirement as previously written could not be executed at all (AM-14). *(verify: results CSV + figure, an archived record of the rule's evaluation at every ratio, and an assertion that no learned-system row exists at a ratio outside the two named here)*
- **ER-4** — **Task-training ablation.** The semantic reconstruction head MUST also be scored through the frozen `params.reference_classifier` (BR-8), separating gain attributable to joint coding from gain attributable to a task-trained classifier. Reported as a distinct `system` value. *(verify: results CSV containing the ablation rows)*
- **ER-5** — Every experiment MUST emit rows matching `params.artifacts.csv_schema` exactly — same columns, same order — alongside the per-image file required by SR-18. *(verify: schema validation script over all result CSVs)*
- **ER-6** — Evaluation on `params.evaluation.test_subset_size` images is permitted for sweeps only; `params.evaluation.full_test_split_required_for` MUST use the full split, and the `test_subset` column MUST record which was used. *(verify: schema test asserting the flag)*
- **ER-7** — Every number appearing in the thesis MUST be traceable to a `run_id` and `git_commit` in a committed CSV. *(verify: audit script resolving each reported figure to its rows)*
- **ER-8** — If a hypothesis in §2 is unsupported, the negative result MUST be reported with the same rigour as a positive one, together with the diagnostic evidence. Weakening the baseline to manufacture support is prohibited. *(verify: review against BR-4 sweep artifacts and BR-11 overhead tables)*
- **ER-9** — **Task-aware digital control.** A third system MUST be built and evaluated at matched `k`, sharing every element in `params.digital_semantic_control.shared_with_learned` with the learned JSCC system and differing from it **only** in `params.digital_semantic_control.differs_only_in`: features taken at `params.digital_semantic_control.transmit_layer` are quantised per `params.digital_semantic_control.quantiser` at a width selected from `params.digital_semantic_control.quantiser_bits_grid` on the validation split (DEC-12), entropy-coded per `params.digital_semantic_control.entropy_coder`, and carried over the same `params.baseline.channel_code` chain as the classical baseline with its transport configuration tuned per `params.digital_semantic_control.transport_tuning`. It MUST be scored by `params.digital_semantic_control.scored_by` — a task head architecturally identical to the learned system's — **not** by the frozen `params.reference_classifier`, which consumes images and cannot read a feature stream (AM-5). Matched `k` fixes the feature budget directly: transmitted feature count × quantiser width + entropy-coder and container overhead MUST fit the same `params.baseline.budget_rule` payload the classical baseline receives. Rationale: without a control that is task-aware *and* digital, the learned-versus-classical gap conflates task-aware representation with joint coding and §1 claim 2 cannot be attributed (H4); and unless the control shares the learned system's front end, a measured difference could equally be architecture, capacity or training objective rather than the channel interface. This is the primary novelty claim of DEC-13. *(verify: results CSV rows under a distinct `system` value at the same k as ER-1, plus an architecture-diff artifact showing that only `params.digital_semantic_control.differs_only_in` separates the two systems)*
- **ER-10** — **Paired inference.** The §2 hypotheses MUST be decided on **paired per-image outcomes** (SR-18), not on the overlap of two independent intervals: `params.evaluation.paired_test` for the point decision and `params.evaluation.ci` with `params.evaluation.bootstrap_resamples` for the interval on the accuracy *difference*, with the image-level bootstrap nested inside the seed hierarchy so `params.evaluation.train_seeds` and `params.evaluation.channel_seeds` contribute as separate variance components. Rationale: both systems see identical images and noise draws, so a paired test is both the natural and the far more powerful analysis — a three-seed Student-t interval has two degrees of freedom and would demand roughly a five-point gap to clear non-overlap. Three further rules make the seed hierarchy honest, since `params.evaluation.bootstrap_resamples` resamples images and cannot manufacture training-run evidence that three seeds do not contain (AM-11): the **classical arm has no training-seed dimension** — it is never trained — so the training-seed variance component belongs to the learned arm alone and a classical result MUST NOT be replicated across seed cells and counted as independent baseline runs; `params.evaluation.paired_test` MUST be computed **within** a seed cell and never pooled across cells, which would treat repeated measurements of the same images as independent; and each seed's accuracy-vs-SNR curve MUST be reported separately alongside the between-seed range, so the reader sees training-run spread rather than inferring it from an interval that mostly reflects image count. ER-10 also computes `params.evaluation.h1_effect_size` and `params.evaluation.gap_trend_test` for §2's H1 and H3. *(verify: inference script reproducing every reported interval from the per-image files, with a unit test on synthetic data of known effect size, and a test that no pooled-across-seeds McNemar statistic is emitted)*
